narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To demonstrate the historical expansion and subsequent long-term stability of the number of countries possessing nuclear weapons.

units.meaning: At the end of the series, in 2015, there are 9 countries with nuclear weapons.

basis.note: Final table row shows value 9 countries.

accepted_routes: In 2015, nine countries have nuclear weapons.
By the final year shown, the count is 9.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 2015 data value must be readable as 9 countries at the end of the series.
units.temporal_anchor: Today, there are nine countries who have nuclear weapons.
units.reviewer_question: Must the final 2015 value be explicitly stated as 9, or is the flat ending sufficient?

units.meaning: The number of nuclear-armed countries expanded from 1 in 1945 to 10 by 1990, an increase of 9 countries over that period.
accepted_routes: The count grows from 1 to 10 over 1945-1990.
Nine more countries acquire nuclear weapons between 1945 and 1990.
The series expands from a single country in 1945 to ten in 1990.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The series must show a clear rise from the 1945 value of 1 to the 1990 value of 10.
units.temporal_anchor: Historical build-up before the 'Today...' payoff (not present in the reference narration).
units.reviewer_question: Is the full 1-to-10 expansion required, or is it enough to show only the final 9-country plateau?

units.meaning: The maximum number in the series is 10 countries in 1990; no later table year exceeds that value.
accepted_routes: The count peaks at 10 countries in 1990.
1990 is the highest point at ten countries.
The maximum is ten, reached in 1990.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 1990 value must be visibly the highest point and readable as 10 countries.
units.temporal_anchor: Historical build-up / peak moment before 'This number has not increased for decades.'
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly identify 1990 as the peak, or can the peak be left implicit in the line shape?

units.meaning: After the 1990 peak, the count falls to 9 by 1995 and stays at 9 for every later table year through 2015: a 20-year stable plateau with no increase.
units.computation: constant 1995-2015 value = 9; span = 2015 - 1995 = 20 years; 1995-2015 values are all <= 1990 value of 10.
accepted_routes: From 1995 through 2015, the number remains at 9 countries.
The count drops from 10 to 9 after 1990 and then stays flat for 20 years.
There is no increase in the number of nuclear-armed countries after 1990, with 9 countries from 1995 onward.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 1995-2015 span must be visibly flat at 9 countries after the 1990 peak.
units.temporal_anchor: This number has not increased for decades.
units.reviewer_question: Should the stability claim be anchored to 1995 (start of 9-country plateau) or to 1990 (last peak)?

units.meaning: South Africa is listed among the 10 countries in 1990 but is absent from the 9-country list from 1995 onward; this is the only listed country difference across the 1990-to-1995 drop.

basis.note: countries column still excludes South Africa.

units.computation: 1990 countries list minus 1995 countries list = {South Africa}; 1990 value 10 - 1995 value 9 = 1 country difference.
accepted_routes: South Africa appears in the 1990 list but not from 1995 onward.
The drop from 10 to 9 countries matches South Africa leaving the listed set.
South Africa is the country omitted between the 1990 and 1995 lists.
units.visual_evidence_rule: If country names are shown, South Africa must appear for 1990 and be absent for 1995-2015.
units.temporal_anchor: Optional explanatory beat at the 1990-to-1995 transition (not in the reference narration).
units.reviewer_question: Is naming South Africa as the 1990-to-1995 difference required, or is it optional detail?

optional_valid: The 1955-1960 plateau at 3 countries and the 1970-1975 plateau at 6 countries.
Pakistan and North Korea first appear in the 1990 countries list.
The 1990 list contains 10 named countries: USA, Russia, UK, France, China, Israel, India, South Africa, Pakistan, and North Korea.
unsupported_to_avoid: Claiming the count increases after 2015 or that 9 is still the count in any later year not in the table.
Claiming South Africa's removal caused the decline (causal language beyond the table's list change).
Using percentages or shares when the table's unit is countries.
Claiming all nine countries have equal nuclear arsenals or that only the named countries have ever possessed nuclear weapons outside the table.
notes: The key required shape is expansion to a 1990 peak of 10 countries followed by a 1995-2015 plateau at 9; the endpoint 9 and no-increase stability are both obligatory, while the South Africa identity explanation is useful but optional.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
